hed: Alpha Ind: The Brightest Beacon in Indus
dek: A luminous star guiding astronomers and stargazers alike, Alpha Ind holds a prominent place in its constellation.
body: Alpha Ind, also designated as α Ind, is a notable star situated within the constellation Indus. Its celestial coordinates place it at approximately 20.26 hours in right ascension and -47.29 degrees in declination, making it a prominent feature in the southern sky. As a figure star, Alpha Ind serves as a key marker in various celestial charts and star maps, appreciated for its brightness and position. This star belongs to the family of stellar objects known for their importance in navigation and astronomical observation. Though detailed information regarding its distance, magnitude, or spectral type is generally curated from wider surveys, Alpha Ind is recognized for its stable luminosity and clear visibility for observers in the southern hemisphere. The star's cultural and navigational significance has historically been linked to its consistent position within the constellation Indus, often aiding in orientation for both ancient sailors and modern astronomers. With its specific catalog identifiers, such as the Hipparcos number HIP 101772, Alpha Ind has been accurately mapped and studied within the broader framework of stellar catalogs. Its role as a figure star means it also features in the traditional constellation asterisms, serving as a visual cornerstone in the pattern that helps identify the shape of Indus across the night sky. Its steady appearance and notable brightness continue to attract interest from both amateur stargazers and professional astronomers, making Alpha Ind an enduring beacon in the galaxy of stars. Observing this star offers a glimpse into the grandeur of the cosmos and represents an accessible point of reference for those exploring the depths of our universe.
